newsitem.title: BELGIUM: LME's King proposes measures to boost tin contract.
newsitem.headline: LME's King proposes measures to boost tin contract.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) chief-executive David King told a World Tin Conference that the LME suggested four areas in which the contract's stagnation could be converted into further growth.
Turnover on the London Metal Exchange's (LME) tin contract has stabilised at about 1.1 million lots a year after growing steadily from about 100,000 lots in 1989.

The tin industry needed to be better informed so as to make better use of the LME and its tin contract to hedge price risk, set reference prices and provide storage facilities, King told the conference held by the International Tin Research Institute.
The LME's tin contract must match industry needs as closely as possible, King said, adding that a new and enlarged LME tin committee, with more industry representatives, would be announced this week.
The locations of the LME's 31 tin warehouses in 11 countries were being reviewed to see if they met industry needs.
Finally, King said that the LME would implement the six recommendations by the British Securities and Investments Board (SIB) by the end of the year.
"(This) will result in the creation of an all round stronger, safer and more transparent LME, better able to serve the needs of the world's tin industry," he said.
King noted that the "tin crisis" of 1985, unlike the Sumitomo Affair concerning copper dealings, had one major difference.
"...the Tin Crisis nearly brought the LME to its knees, many members leaving the market and trading volumes collapsing dramatically," he said.
